Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
30 September 2026 .
Brent $ 103.58 + 0.79 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports three more tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have surfaced through delayed UKMTO reports, with unknown munitions striking three vessels.

02 Iran is reviewing the US ceasefire counterproposal, per WKRC and KBOI, with Strait of Hormuz terms still unclear.

03 Brent stood at $103.58, up 0.79% over 24 hours, as of 20:30 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a contested and dangerous corridor. gCaptain reports that three additional tanker attacks have surfaced through delayed UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting, with unknown munitions striking three vessels; the attacker has not been identified. This follows the Tuesday attacks already reported in earlier coverage. CNBC reports that crude oil exports through the strait have reached prewar levels but that fuel shipments remain constrained, cautioning that the recovery relies on US military protection of tankers in the Persian Gulf. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. On the diplomatic side, Iran is reviewing the US ceasefire counterproposal, per WKRC and KBOI, with Strait of Hormuz terms still unresolved. The International Business Times reports that Iran received the US ceasefire counterproposal shortly before tankers were reportedly hit in the strait. Brent stood at $103.58, up 0.79% over 24 hours, as of 20:30 UTC. The site's 61 indexed events in the past 24 hours reflect continued operational pressure across the waterway. Shipping and insurance professionals should note that incident reporting continues to surface on a delay through UKMTO, meaning the current picture of attacks may be incomplete at any given moment. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
